studies.label: Think-aloud evaluation of EQ-HWB-9 recall and proxy perspective among carers of people with dementia
studies.family_rationale: The main contribution is qualitative evidence about interpretation of the EQ-HWB-9 recall period and proxy-reporting perspective. These are content-validity and response-process questions. The study did not produce new instrument content or a value set.

items.statement: Carers used two main retrieval strategies: extending the recall period to include significant events or self-report, and using earlier behavior and personal history to contextualize recent behavior.
source: input/projects/1557-RA/papers/doi_10.1007_s11136-026-04230-y.xml, Results > Use and interpretation of the recall period in retrieval, opening paragraph and Strategy 1–2 subsections

items.statement: Adherence to the 7-day recall period was more consistent for observable or readily verbalized domains. For less observable feelings, carers more often used earlier events, personality, mannerisms, or indirect behavioral indicators.
source: input/projects/1557-RA/papers/doi_10.1007_s11136-026-04230-y.xml, Results > Strategy 1: extending the recall period to capture significant events

items.statement: Carers used different response strategies across item formats. For difficulty items they averaged behavior, emphasized the most difficult moments, or considered frequency. For most frequency items they counted either days or occurrences within the recall period.

items.statement: All carers used their own observations and judgments, consistent with the proxy–proxy perspective. Nearly half also imagined how the person with dementia would answer, consistent with the proxy–patient perspective. No carer used only the proxy–patient perspective.

items.statement: Wording changes may be needed to support consistent use of the 7-day recall period, especially for less observable items.

Proxy-perspective instructions and adherence need further consideration. Instructions and item wording may need revision to improve recall consistency and applicability of the proxy EQ-HWB-9 in dementia.
Convenience recruitment through a webpage linked to an online dementia course may have selected people with a personal interest in dementia or higher digital literacy.
The study included only people living in Australia who spoke English, so the findings may not generalize to other populations or patient groups that require proxy reporting.
Evidence about cognitive processes was limited to what participants verbalized during think-aloud and probing, and emotional factors may have caused omission of sensitive topics.
The study did not determine how easy carers found it to remember the person's ability to self-report, which may affect the choice of proxy perspective.
The study did not explore in depth how relationship type, carer role, cultural background, or prior proxy-reporting experience influenced the findings.
Nearly all participating carers were female, although the authors stated that it was unclear whether this was a limitation.
